issues.title: Missing semicolons in variable declarations
issues.description: The rule requires all JavaScript and TypeScript statements to end with explicit semicolons, but lines 88-90 rely on automatic semicolon insertion (ASI) instead

issues.title: Missing dependency in useEffect causes stale clamp detection
issues.description: The CommentContent component's useEffect hook has an empty dependency array, but it uses item.html to determine if content should be clamped. When a comment's HTML content changes (e.g., after an edit or when new data is loaded), the clamp detection won't re-run. This means the 'Show more' button may appear when it shouldn't or disappear when it should still be visible, creating a poor user experience. The dependency array should include item.html to ensure the clamp detection re-runs whenever the content changes.

issues.title: Filter button becomes non-functional when onAddFilter is undefined
issues.description: The conditional check for rendering the post title button was changed from `item.post?.id && item.post?.title && onAddFilter` to `item.post?.id && item.post?.title`, removing the onAddFilter null check. However, the button's onClick handler still calls onAddFilter('post', item.post!.id). Since onAddFilter is now a required prop in the TypeScript signature but the runtime check was removed, if onAddFilter is ever undefined or null at runtime, clicking the post title button will throw an error and crash the component. The original three-part condition was protecting against this scenario.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: {item.post?.id && item.post?.title ? ( ) : ( Unknown post )}

issues.title: Inconsistent conditional rendering pattern for feature image
issues.description: The feature image rendering logic was changed from a ternary expression with explicit null return (`condition ? : null`) to a logical AND operator (`condition && `). While functionally similar in most cases, this creates an inconsistency: when item.post?.feature_image is falsy (like an empty string ''), the logical AND will render the falsy value (empty string) instead of rendering nothing. This could lead to unexpected DOM nodes or React warnings. The original ternary with explicit null was more defensive and clearer about the intent to render nothing when the condition is false.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: {item.post?.feature_image && ( )}

issues.title: Delete comment functionality completely removed from UI
issues.description: The PR removes the dropdown menu item that allowed users to delete comments, making the delete functionality completely inaccessible through the UI. While all the backend infrastructure remains intact (AlertDialog component, confirmDelete function, deleteComment mutation, commentToDelete state), there is no button or menu item that calls setCommentToDelete to trigger the deletion flow. This is a critical functional regression that removes an essential moderation capability for administrators. Users can no longer delete comments through the interface, even though the API endpoint and confirmation dialog are still present in the code.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: {item.post?.url && ( View post )} {item.member?.id && ( View member )}

issues.title: Missing semicolons in CommentContent hook declarations
issues.description: The added variable/state declarations rely on automatic semicolon insertion (ASI). The codebase rule requires explicit semicolons at the end of all statements.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25745 - Redesigned comment moderation list layout

structured_output.summary:
This PR replaces the comment moderation table in the Posts app with a stacked, comment-like row layout. Each row now shows the author (with a filter button), a relative timestamp with a tooltip, the post title (as a filter button), a clamped body with a Show more/less toggle, Hide/Show buttons, reply/like/report counts, and an overflow menu. A post feature image is added to the right column. The API surface is extended to return `post.feature_image` through the comments output mapper, the admin-x-framework `Comment` type is updated, and the e2e snapshots are adjusted to match.

The layout work is reasonable and the data-plumbing side is consistent. However, the rewrite silently drops the "Delete comment" action. The row's dropdown menu no longer contains it, and the confirmation `AlertDialog` is left in the file with no code path that opens it, so moderators can no longer delete comments from this screen. Separately, the row loses its link to the post editor, and the expand/collapse control can get stuck in the expanded state after a window resize. I would not merge until the delete regression is fixed.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The removal of the delete action is a functional regression in a moderation tool, and nothing in the repo tests it. The dead AlertDialog wiring suggests it was an accident rather than a decision. The remaining issues (lost editor navigation, the resize bug, accessibility gaps) are real but less severe and can be fixed in the same pass.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, the Posts app's comments screen (`comments.tsx`) rendered `CommentsList` as a virtualized table with Comment, Author, Post, Date, and Actions columns. Each row's actions were a Hide/Show button plus a dropdown that included View post, Filter by post, Filter by author, and Delete comment. Delete opened an AlertDialog, and the dialog's confirm called `useDeleteComment`. Data comes from the Ghost core comments API, where `serializers/output/mappers/comments.js` controls which post fields are returned, and the client type lives in `admin-x-framework/api/comments.ts`.

The PR changes the presentation layer only, plus one added field. `CommentsList` now renders each row as a stacked card: a header line (author, timestamp, post), a clamped body via the new `CommentContent` component, an action row with Hide/Show, count badges, and an overflow menu, and a right-hand feature-image cell. The mapper and type gain `feature_image` on the post. The delete dialog and its state are still present, but the only entry point that set `commentToDelete` has been removed.
steps: Entry point: `comments.tsx` fetches comments and passes `items`, pagination props, and `onAddFilter` into `CommentsList`. `onAddFilter` is now required, which lets the old `&&` guards be removed.

Data boundary: `ghost/core` output mapper `comments.js` adds `feature_image` to the serialized `post` object, and `admin-x-framework`'s `Comment` type declares it as optional. The snapshot diffs are the observable effect of this change.

Row structure in `comments-list.tsx`: each `TableRow` is a CSS grid with a `TableCell` for the main content and a second `TableCell` for the feature image. The main cell holds a header line, the new `CommentContent` body, and an action row.
Body clamping: `CommentContent` clamps HTML to two lines with `line-clamp-2`, measures `scrollHeight` against `clientHeight` on mount and resize, and shows an `ExpandButton` only when clamped.
Actions: Hide/Show stay inline. The overflow menu now holds only View post and View member. Delete is no longer reachable, though its dialog and state are still in the file.

findings.title: Delete comment action removed; confirmation dialog is now unreachable
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, restore a delete entry point for comments. The dropdown menu inside each row (around lines 326-357) has lost its "Delete comment" item, but the `AlertDialog` (around lines 366-384), `confirmDelete`, and `commentToDelete` state are still in the file. Add back a `handleDeleteClick`-style handler that calls `setCommentToDelete(item)`, and render a destructive `DropdownMenuItem` for it when `item.status !== 'deleted'`, separated by a `DropdownMenuSeparator`. Restore the `DropdownMenuSeparator` import too. Follow the original implementation in the base commit (`git show 8281bbf2:apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`).

findings.title: Post title no longer links to the post editor
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, the post title in each comment row (around lines 236-246) is now a filter button only. Restore a link to the post editor (`#/editor/post/${item.post.id}`) in the row or the overflow menu, as the base commit did. Keep the post-filter action as well if the design needs it. Add an "Edit post" item to the existing `DropdownMenuContent` (around lines 329-357), or use a secondary link next to the title, and match the link styling used elsewhere in the file.

findings.title: Show less control disappears after resizing while expanded
findings.fixPrompt: In `CommentContent` in `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx` (around lines 87-120), the clamp detection drops the Show-less button after a resize while expanded. Fix it so the `ExpandButton` stays visible whenever `isExpanded` is true. For example, only update `isClamped` when `!isExpanded`, or keep `isClamped` true while expanded. Also re-run the measurement when `item.html` changes by adding it to the `useEffect` dependency array. Keep the existing resize listener and its cleanup.

findings.title: No tests cover the redesigned comment list
findings.body:
The only test changes are snapshot updates for the API output (`comments.test.js.snap`, `activity-feed.test.js.snap`). A grep for `comment-list-row`, `comments-list`, and "Delete comment" across `apps/posts` finds only the component itself. The following paths have no coverage:

- The delete flow, which is the regression above. A test would have caught it.
- The clamp/expand toggle, including the resize edge case above.
- The conditional rendering of Hide vs Show based on `item.status`.
- The fallbacks for a missing member, a missing post, and a missing `feature_image`.

Snapshot changes also confirm the API shape but nothing about the UI.
findings.fixPrompt: Add component tests for `CommentsList` in `apps/posts` (for example under `apps/posts/test`, following the existing test setup in that app). Cover: (1) the overflow menu offers Delete and confirming it calls `useDeleteComment` with the right id; (2) Hide/Show render based on `item.status`; (3) the Show more/less control appears only when the content overflows, and stays available after a resize while expanded; (4) member and post fallbacks render when those fields are missing. Mock the admin-x-framework comment hooks rather than the component under test.

findings.title: Icon-only overflow button has no accessible name
findings.body:
The new ellipsis trigger renders only `<LucideIcon.Ellipsis />` with no `aria-label` or visually hidden text, so screen readers announce it as an unnamed button. The old button had a `MoreVertical` icon with the same problem, but the PR is a good place to fix it since it changes the trigger.

::code{file="apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx" lines="320-327"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, the overflow `Button` wrapping `<LucideIcon.Ellipsis />` (around lines 320-327) has no accessible name. Add `aria-label="More actions"` (or an equivalent visually hidden label) to the button.

findings.title: Falsy template-literal values leak into class names
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, replace the `${item.status === 'hidden' && 'text-muted-foreground'}` fragments in the `CommentContent` body class (around line 112) and the member button class (around line 194) with a ternary (`? 'text-muted-foreground' : ''`) or with `cn(...)` from `@tryghost/shade`, so the literal string `false` never reaches the DOM.

findings.title: Overflow menu rows now link to the member profile only through the menu
findings.body: Moving member and post navigation into the overflow menu, and turning the inline member and post text into filter buttons, is a visible behavior change. Reviewers should confirm that filtering is the intended primary action for those two items. The point above about the post editor is the one that needs a decision.

findings.title: Required onAddFilter removes dead guards
findings.body: Making `onAddFilter` required is a good cleanup. The old `onAddFilter && ...` guards were dead code because `comments.tsx` always passes `handleAddFilter`, and the type now says so. The same applies to the `item.post?.id && onAddFilter` menu items that were removed.

findings.title: API and type change is minimal and consistent
findings.body: Adding `feature_image` in both places is consistent. The mapper's `postFields` list controls the output, and the TypeScript type is optional, which matches what the API returns when a post has no image. The snapshot `content-length` values move by the byte count you would expect from one extra key, which makes it likely that the snapshots were regenerated from a real run rather than hand-edited. The image is also public post data, so exposing it to the admin API does not add a new privacy surface.

findings.title: Counts and hidden state are conveyed visually and through tooltips
findings.body: Replies, likes, and reports each get a labeled tooltip, and hidden comments get a text label ("Hidden from members") instead of an icon-only treatment. Both are clearer than the old table, and the reports count is highlighted when non-zero. Consider making the tooltip text visible to assistive tech via `aria-label` on the counts, since the numbers alone are ambiguous to screen readers.
